title: Wire the judge obligation into the live cells add path
action: jo-1 built assert_judge_obligation (obligation.rs:325) and tested it at the function level, but never called it from the live path — validate.rs:188 calls assert_regen_obligation only, so the guard is inert exactly the way pattern-20260805 (source that ships without being called) and the present rung of the evidence ladder describe. Call assert_judge_obligation beside assert_regen_obligation in the same validator, matching how the regen refusal composes into the whole-batch validation (every cell checked before any is written, one call naming every problem). Then prove it END TO END, not at the function level: a test that drives the real cells add entry point (the same out-of-process idiom the existing add tests use) with (a) a tiny cell touching packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/hooks and asserts the refusal names both escapes and writes nothing, (b) the same cell at lane standard and asserts it is accepted, (c) the same tiny cell carrying judge_obligation_ack and asserts it is accepted with the ack recorded on the stored cell, (d) a batch where one cell trips the obligation and asserts the WHOLE batch is refused with nothing written. Also raise the pattern rung: docs/knowledge/patterns/20260812-a-guard-and-its-tests-are-one-model-*.md gains bee.evidence wired plus bee.evidence_ref naming this guard, once the end-to-end tests are green (frontmatter key order matters: evidence and evidence_ref sit after critical and before signature; run bee knowledge check and expect no not_canonical on that file).

truths: The refusal fires through the real cells add path, not just the function
A tripped obligation refuses the whole batch and writes nothing
judge_obligation_ack is stored on the accepted cell
The pattern moves to evidence wired only after the end-to-end tests are green

Raised pattern-20260812 to evidence: wired.
